title: Bakery and Tide
premise: Beatrix Almeida, a single mother running Salt Hollow's only bookshop, learns her late grandmother left her half of the failing Almeida Orchard—co-owned with Jonah Reyes, the boy who left town twelve years ago and never wrote back. Forced to share harvest season on the stubborn land, Beatrix and Jonah rebuild an old almost-love while fighting a developer's offer that would save them both financially but erase everything their families built. At the climax, Beatrix must choose between selling her half and trusting Jonah's plan to keep the orchard alive; she chooses trust, and in the epilogue-tinged final chapter, Jonah stays after the last train leaves, choosing belonging over escape.
about_author: Noor Vasquez is a former pastry chef turned novelist who writes small-town romances about second chances and inherited places. She lives near the coast with her daughter and an untidy herb garden.

chapters.title: The Deed in the Drawer
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Sorting her grandmother's estate, Beatrix discovers the orchard deed bearing two names: hers and Jonah Reyes, the boy who vanished after one unforgettable summer. Her daughter Poppy asks why Mama never talks about him. Emotional beat: grief cracked open by shock; the past refuses to stay past tense.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Register
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah returns to Salt Hollow to sell his inherited half, only to find his first stop is the bookshop—and Beatrix behind the counter, older, guarded, unmistakable. Neither says what they both remember. Emotional beat: recognition as ambush; old wounds wearing new faces.

chapters.title: Terms of Harvest
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A lawyer forces co-ownership terms: neither can sell without the other's agreement until season's end. Jonah proposes they run the harvest together, split proceeds, then part. Beatrix agrees, telling herself it's business. Emotional beat: wary truce; proximity disguised as practicality.

chapters.title: Cider and Small Hours
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Late nights pressing cider thaw into real conversation—Jonah confesses why he left: family debt, shame, letters he was too proud to send. Beatrix admits she read the silence as rejection. Poppy bonds with Jonah over apple grafting. Emotional beat: tenderness rekindling under exhaustion.

chapters.title: The Developer's Letter
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. A resort developer offers double market value for the whole orchard—enough to clear Jonah's lingering debts and fund Beatrix's leaking bookshop roof. He hides the letter, ashamed of how tempted he is. Emotional beat: guilt curdling hope; money as a test of identity.

chapters.title: Frost Warning
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Beatrix finds the hidden letter during a frost emergency and feels the summer's warmth collapse into betrayal-by-omission. They fight in the packing shed, both saying cruel true things. Poppy overhears. Emotional beat: rupture; the past tense snapping shut again.

chapters.title: What the Trees Remember
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. A discovered ledger shows their grandparents ran the orchard together for forty years through worse fights than this—the deed's 'impossible' co-ownership was deliberate, a promise. Each privately confronts what they're actually afraid of losing. Emotional beat: reframing inheritance as invitation, not burden.

chapters.title: The Last Train Schedule
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Jonah books a departure for after the harvest festival, telling himself leaving is mercy. But drafting a goodbye note to Poppy, he realizes he's writing to a family, not a fling. He tears it up. Emotional beat: the cost of invisibility finally outweighs its safety.

chapters.title: Harvest Festival
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. At the festival, the developer makes a public final offer before the crowd. Beatrix, instead of answering, publicly commits her half to keeping the orchard working—an act of faith she can't guarantee Jonah will match. Emotional beat: climax; choosing trust without assurance.

chapters.title: After the Last Train Leaves
chapters.summary: Alternating POV closing with Beatrix. Jonah declines the sale, signs a five-year co-stewardship, and misses the train on purpose. In the empty station parking lot, Beatrix waits anyway—and he walks back to her. The bookshop gets a new roof; the orchard gets a future. Emotional beat: resolution; staying as the bravest verb.
